free_tier.stated: No free tier; a 7-day trial with a paid ChatGPT subscription. Minimum monthly spend USD 15.

retention.stated: Persistent disks are included; 100 GiB of filesystem usage per 2 vCPUs, and additional disk at USD 0.08/GiB/month.

egress.terms: 200 GiB of network bandwidth included on Personal; additional bandwidth USD 0.05/GiB.

interface_detail: SSH into the VM as root, with apt and systemd; sign-in is through a Google account in the browser
tooling: ssh, apt, systemd, and a web agent named Shelley for coding; a pool of vCPUs is reserved and shared by the VMs
chaining: the pool model is the unusual part: 50 VMs share one 2 vCPU / 4 GiB reservation, so a fleet of idle sandboxes costs the same as one. It composes with a scheduler that starts many short-lived workers

limits.value: 200 GiB of network bandwidth a month on Personal; USD 0.05/GiB beyond

limits_note: The pool model means the bill is a floor plus hourly overage, not a machine price.
binding_note: The binding constraint is the USD 15 minimum monthly spend, which no shape reduces; bandwidth is the metered wall behind it.

identity_cost.detail: A paid plan implies a card; the pricing page states no card, hold or debit terms. The 7-day trial is gated on a paid ChatGPT subscription. Unverified.

reliability_note: No reliability event observed the trial is time-boxed at 7 days.

evidence.proved: '7-day trial with a paid ChatGPT subscription', quoted; Personal plan USD 15 a month for 2 vCPUs / 4 GiB, 50 VMs, 100 GiB of filesystem and 200 GiB of bandwidth
'You reserve a pool of vCPUs and memory, and your VMs share it', 'SSH in, you are root, you have apt and systemd', quoted

quoted: 'Personal ... $15 / month ... Pool size 2 vCPUs / 4 GiB memory ... 50 VMs ... 100 GiB of filesystem usage included ... 200 GiB of network bandwidth'
quoted: 'Minimum Monthly Spend | $15'; 'Additional disk | $0.08 / GiB / month'; 'Additional bandwidth | $0.05 / GiB'; 'KVM-isolated VMs | Included'; 'Persistent disks | Included'

notes: USD 15 a month is the floor and it buys 2 vCPU / 4 GiB spread over up to 50 VMs, so the per-VM cost is near zero but the bill is three times the budget. Standalone VMs are priced at USD 0.105/hour per 2 vCPU / 4 GiB for accounts above the minimum, which is USD 76.65 at 730 h. Egress arithmetic: USD 0.05/GiB x 1000 GB = USD 50 per TB beyond the 200 GiB allowance. Not established: the payment method and hold.

shape.note: a pool of 2 vCPU / 4 GiB shared across up to 50 VMs, 100 GiB of filesystem included

extras.price_arithmetic: USD 15.00 a month minimum, billed monthly, so 24/7 = USD 15.00 and 10 h/day = USD 15.00. The metered alternative is USD 0.105/hour per 2 vCPU / 4 GiB = USD 76.65 at 730 h.

network_out.ports: managed HTTPS and TLS with custom domains included; raw-port ingress terms not stated on the pricing page

session_cap.note: none stated; VMs persist with their disks

tier: Personal: USD 15/month pool of 2 vCPU / 4 GiB, up to 50 VMs
confidence_note: Plan price, pool size, VM count, disk and bandwidth allowances and the additional-disk and bandwidth rates are quoted from the pricing page read today. Payment method and SSH details beyond the table are not on that page.
